headline: High: gpt-researcher can read files and call external APIs while dagster is a non-runnable orchestrator, creating leakage and cascading-error risk if wired together.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem read/write, or MCP surfaces, so there is no documented automatic instruction bridge from gpt-researcher into dagster. The only plausible pathway is manual handoff or an external shared channel not shown here, so prompt injection risk is limited and uncertain.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies gpt-researcher output into a dagster task definition or config file
IF a shared MCP or message queue is added between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Require manual review before any copied text becomes a dagster asset
Disable any shared MCP bridge
Use a fixed prompt template for dagster tasks
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all handoffs

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher reads local documents and sends queries/reports through external APIs, while dagster is a data-engineering orchestrator with no filesystem read/write of its own. If dagster passes sensitive files into gpt-researcher, those contents can flow to third-party inference or search services, so the pair can leak data in a default research workflow.
conditions: IF dagster supplies local documents or secrets to gpt-researcher inputs
IF gpt-researcher is configured to use OpenAI, Tavily, LangChain, or Gemini APIs
mitigations: Do not route secrets into research inputs
Restrict gpt-researcher to non-sensitive corpora
Rotate API keys used by gpt-researcher
Review outbound destinations before each run
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster is non-runnable and has no write or network capabilities, while gpt-researcher can read files, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress. There is no direct same-directory write conflict shown, but if dagster orchestrates shared mutable resources through gpt-researcher, overlapping control of files or APIs can still collide.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace or shared API-backed resource
IF dagster is extended with write access outside the shown profile
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize access to shared datasets
Avoid concurrent writes to the same report folder
Use per-run resource locks
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations, and dagster is a data orchestrator that could consume those outputs as pipeline inputs. Because dagster has no built-in verification surface in the profile, a bad or hallucinated report can cascade into downstream pipeline decisions or published artifacts without a documented check.
conditions: IF dagster uses gpt-researcher output as authoritative pipeline input
IF no human or automated verification step is inserted between them
mitigations: Require source checks before ingestion
Add a validation step for citations and facts
Block automatic publication from research output
Sample outputs for manual review
requires-engineering: add schema and provenance validation

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher handles local documents, citations, and multiple external APIs, which can create retention and residency issues for regulated content. Dagster itself is open-source and non-runnable here, so the compliance concern is mainly on the gpt-researcher side; the pair becomes risky if dagster routes regulated data into that workflow.
conditions: IF regulated documents or personal data are fed into gpt-researcher
IF the configured API providers retain prompts or outputs beyond policy
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from research jobs
Confirm provider retention settings
Use region-appropriate API endpoints
Log data-class labels per run
requires-engineering: enforce residency and retention policy checks
